text:
maya: Heads-up — opened a quick thread for the embeddings API decisions we discussed in async. Need alignment on: accepted input types, truncation semantics, and the exact output vector shape we return in batch responses.

maya: PR linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/456 — it's small, adds strict input validation + truncation hook.

devin: looking now. quick q: do we accept bytes/base64 payloads or only UTF-8 strings? Some customers want binary blobs.

maya: goal is to accept text/strings only in 1st pass. If we add base64 later, it'll be opt-in via header `X-Embed-Accept-B64: true`. For now we should reject non-string items with 400.

sam: +1 for progressive opt-in. Also we need clear behavior for empty string vs null: empty string => valid input (will produce embedding), null => return error for that item but process others?

maya: propose: null items are allowed in a batch and we return `null` vector in same position. That keeps positional alignment. Document this.

li: note on truncation — current runtime truncates to 4096 bytes by default for model X-embed-1536. PR sets truncation at UTF-8 codepoint boundaries and adds a `truncate` query param that accepts `none|smart|hard`.

devin: can you clarify modes?

li: `none` = return 400 if too long. `hard` = cut raw bytes at limit (may break multibyte chars). `smart` = cut at last whitespace before limit preserving codepoint boundaries. Default `smart`.

maya: sample request we want in docs (batch):
```json
{
  "model": "x-embed-1536",
  "inputs": ["short text", "", null, "very long text..."],
  "truncate": "smart"
}
```

maya: sample response shape: array-of-results preserving order: if item succeeded => object with `embedding`: [floats], `len_tokens`: 123; if item null => `embedding: null`, `error`: "null input". Example:
```json
[
  {"embedding": [0.00123, -0.2345, ... 1536 numbers total], "len_tokens": 12},
  {"embedding": [ ... 1536 floats ... ], "len_tokens": 0},
  {"embedding": null, "error": "null input"},
  {"embedding": [ ... 1536 floats ... ], "len_tokens": 4096}
]
```

sam: 1536-dim is fine. pls ensure we never truncate vector output length — always fixed length. Also add a short-circuit for empty string to avoid wasting GPU cycles (return zeros? or real embed?).

devin: we should NOT return zeros for empty string. It hides semantics. Better run model; cheap for small inputs.

maya: agreed, run model. latency impact minimal for tiny inputs and consistent semantics.

li: batch limits: runtime config uses `max_batch_items=1024` and `max_payload_bytes=10_000_000` by default. PR enforces a per-request `inputs` length cap of 2048 items with clear 413 if exceeded. We should sync docs and console.

maya: action items: 1) devin — review PR comments about 400 vs 422 for bad item types. 2) li — add docs snippet for `truncate` and exact byte/token limits. 3) sam — add test case for null-in-batch and positional alignment.

devin: pinged on PR, left comment: prefer 422 for semantic errors (bad item type) and 400 for totally malformed body.

pr-bot: PR #456 CI passed, mergeable after 2 approvals.

maya: ok will incorporate devin's status. If we converge on 422 for per-item type errors, we'll document that and include example responses. Anyone opposed?

sam: fine. I'll add a unit test that expects `[{embedding:null,error:"null input"}]` for a single-null-batch.

li: I'll update runtime default values in the console and add an alert rule so we know if `max_batch_items` gets adjusted at infra layer.

devin: LGTM on approach. merging tomorrow after tests.

maya: thanks — I'll follow up with a short blurb for the changelog and notify docs. :tada:
